title: 2026 Annual Threat Assessment of the U.S. Intelligence Community — Phase 65 Quantum review
publisher: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Quantum reporting pack. The 2026 assessment describes the most direct national-security threats for the coming year, including state competition, cyber activity, space and weapons risks, and the strategic implications of AI and quantum technologies. It is a threat baseline rather than a technology forecast.
key_findings: AI and quantum advances are treated as competitive capabilities with security consequences.
Cyber, space, supply-chain, and weapons risks interact with regional and state threats.
The assessment focuses primarily on near-term threats using information available through March 14, 2026.
why_it_matters: Which records separate quantum research and migration policy from standards, procurement, tested interoperability, accepted cutover, and retired cryptography? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. It provides an intelligence-community demand context for resilient systems, secure adoption, and research priorities across AI, quantum, cyber, and infrastructure.
ftfn_relevance: Supports threat-side context for technology and infrastructure signals.
Helps separate strategic risk claims from capability, budget, and deployment evidence.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The unclassified assessment omits classified evidence and detail.
Threat assessment does not prove that a proposed technology or policy response will be effective.
